page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the cosine formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the formula, then the dot product and the two magnitudes. Both magnitudes are √14 here, which makes the denominator simply 14.
steps.memory_tip: Write the formula, then the dot and the two magnitudes. Both are √14, so the denominator is 14.

recall.must_convey: That cos θ = (a·b)/(|a||b|) is stated, the dot product is 7 and both magnitudes are √14.
accept: cos theta is a dot b over the two magnitudes, the dot product is seven and both lengths are root fourteen
write the cosine formula, dot product seven, magnitudes root fourteen each
use cos theta equals a dot b by mod a mod b
cos theta formula rasi, dot product seven, rendu magnitudes root fourteen
state the formula and work out the three pieces

steps.why: The dot product already contains the angle — dividing by the two lengths is what isolates the cosine from it.
common_mistakes: Adding the magnitudes instead of multiplying.
Sign slip on the middle term of the dot product.

steps.label: Find the angle
steps.margin_note: Second mark. √14 times √14 is 14, so the fraction is 7/14 = 1/2 — and a cosine of a half is a familiar angle.
steps.memory_tip: 7/14 = 1/2, and a cosine of a half is a familiar angle.

recall.must_convey: That cos θ simplifies to 1/2, so θ = 60°.
accept: seven over fourteen is a half and cos sixty is a half so the angle is sixty degrees
cos theta is one half so theta is sixty degrees
the angle comes out as sixty degrees
cos theta half kabatti sixty degrees

steps.why: Root fourteen times root fourteen is just fourteen — recognising that saves computing a decimal and leaves an exact angle.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as cos θ = 1/2 when the ANGLE was asked for.
Reaching for a calculator instead of recognising the standard value.
